title: Unique identifier linking through government ID
description: Government ID is a globally unique identifier that can be used to link this registration data to other systems or databases, potentially enabling cross-system tracking of the parent user.
assumptions: Government ID is stored and potentially shared with third parties

title: Quasi-identifier combination linking
description: The combination of email, name, and government ID can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify the parent user when combined with external data sources.

title: Processing of identified personal data
description: The authentication service explicitly requests and processes identified personal data including name, email, government ID, and password during parent registration.
assumptions: The system is designed to collect and store this identified information

title: Unique identifier processing
description: Government ID is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject that is collected and processed during registration.
assumptions: Government ID is stored in the authentication service database

title: Quasi-identifier combination
description: Email, name, and government ID together form quasi-identifiers that can uniquely identify the parent user within the system context.
assumptions: These attributes are stored together and can be correlated

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Government ID is highly sensitive personal data that may be collected beyond what is strictly necessary for basic authentication service functionality.
assumptions: Authentication service may not require government ID for core functionality

title: Excessive data volume
description: Multiple data types (email, password, name, government ID, six-digit code) are collected during registration, potentially exceeding functional necessity.
assumptions: All data types may not be required for authentication service core functionality

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: Personal data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched beyond what is necessary to achieve authentication service functionality.
assumptions: Data may be used for profiling, marketing, or other purposes beyond authentication

title: Unawareness of data processing
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of how their personal data (especially government ID) is collected, processed, stored, or potentially shared.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be clear or comprehensive

title: Lack of data subject control over preferences
description: The parent user may lack control to set preferences or provide granular consent regarding how their personal data is processed during registration.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be limited or not granular

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting government ID and multiple data types may violate GDPR data minimization principle if not strictly necessary for authentication service functionality.
assumptions: GDPR applies to this authentication service

title: Invalid consent risk
description: Personal data collection may not rely on valid consent if consent is not properly obtained, informed, or freely given during registration.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be inadequate
